content:
Want to use Signal on multiple devices at the same time? This encrypted messaging service is now making it easier for users to use it across platforms, including between iPhones and other devices.

Signal users can now link another iPhone to an existing Signal account, rather than being limited to using only an iPad as a companion mobile device.

The company also announced support for Android linking today, stating: "We are expanding the ability to link devices on iOS so you can link an iPhone to your Signal account, and our support for iPad will continue going forward."

When linking another iPhone, users can choose whether to transfer all message history and media files stored in the past 45 days.

Signal said the entire transfer process uses the same "linked devices and sync" technology as iPad and desktop devices (including Signal for Mac), with end-to-end encryption used throughout.

This expansion is particularly useful for users who need to keep work and personal iPhones separate, as well as for users who need to test multiple devices.

This change also brings Signal's multi-device experience closer to the Apple Messages ecosystem, enabling seamless conversations between iPhone, iPad and Mac.

Signal iOS version 8.22 is now available on the App Store. Signal also recently introduced a username feature, allowing users to contact each other without sharing phone numbers.
